name: Bottle of mercury
description: A small glass bottle holding a heavy pool of liquid metal under a black screw cap.
notes: Modelled as the bottle a player picks up, 32 mm across and 62 mm tall, holding 30 mL of mercury in mirror-silver under glass-clear; the whole bottle is one item, as liquids are, so the 0.45 kg mass is 405 g of metal plus the bottle. CHECK mass and volume: the reference counts one millilitre per unit. The tile draws the glass opaque, so the metal shows only in game.

name: Sheet of glass
description: A large sheet of plain window glass. It breaks easily.
notes: 1220 by 915 mm and 2.4 mm thick, lying flat, with syrup-green edge bands for glass's green edge and a paper sticker. It sets a 4 mm grain, so the sheet draws one voxel thick; that is the box/volume excess. Size follows the 1220 mm side and is too big for any bag; it is meant to be carried by hand, which needs a carried-item rule the schema does not have yet.

name: Pane of bullet-resistant glass
description: A thick square of laminated glass in a steel frame, made to stop bullets.
notes: 305 mm square and 57 mm thick: glass-clear with three plastic-frosted interlayers, in a steel-grey channel frame whose lips cover 12 mm of each face, which carries the reference's steel.

name: Sheet of bullet-resistant glass
description: A large sheet of laminated bullet-resistant glass edged in steel.
notes: 1220 by 915 mm and 19 mm thick, so the reference's 21.2 L volume and 45.9 kg mass hold; a sheet that size two inches thick would weigh about three times as much. Steel-grey edge strip, two plastic-frosted interlayers and a yellow rating stripe along the front. Size as for the plain sheet: carried by hand.

name: Sheet of tempered glass
description: A large sheet of tempered safety glass, with the maker's mark etched in one corner. It shatters into small blunt pieces.
notes: 1220 by 965 mm and 6 mm thick, which matches the reference's 7.07 L; syrup-green edge bands and a plastic-frosted etched mark. The 4 mm grain draws it 8 mm thick, the box/volume excess. Size as for the plain sheet: carried by hand.

name: Can of red paint
description: A gallon can of red paint with a wire handle.
notes: A gallon can 168 mm across and 192 mm tall with rolled rims, a pressed lid, a wire bail with a plastic grip, a label band in the paint's colour and a run of paint from the rim. The whole can is one item, as liquids are: 15 of the reference's 325 g units plus about 0.4 kg of can make 5.3 kg. CHECK mass and volume: the reference counts per unit. The box/volume excess is the bail. Each colour is its own draft on this model with a finishes map for the paint slot.

name: Door viewer
description: A brass door viewer: a short barrel with a wide lens at one end and a screw-in eyepiece at the other.
notes: 14 mm across and 48 mm long, lying on its side: brass-polished barrel and lens flange, a brass-dull slotted eyepiece sleeve, glass-clear lenses. CHECK VOLUME: the reference's 250 mL is far above a door viewer's size; the model keeps the real size.

name: Roll of insect screen
description: A roll of fine mesh for screening out insects, wound on a card core.
notes: 300 mm wide and 66 mm across, wound on a paperboard core with a strip of tape, its loose end lying 70 mm out in front; mesh-black with plastic-charcoal winding lines on the ends. The box/volume excess is the loose end. Drawn as a roll, as the reference shows it.
